primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Non-conviction sealing: not-guilty, no-bill, and no-probable-cause records are to be sealed by the Commissioner of Probation and the court/probation offices unless the defendant makes a written request not to seal; dismissals and nolle prosequi require a court petition and a finding that substantial justice would best be served by sealing.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.citation: Boston Municipal Court Department Amended Standing Order No. 1-09
primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: The Boston Municipal Court Department permits a single consolidated petition to seal three or more criminal records from two or more BMC divisions, under a Standing Order revised after Pon to conform to the new legal standard. It is a local implementation of the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing remedy, not a separate statewide remedy.
The good-cause narrative across all listed records is participant-authored through structured prompts against the Pon factors.

verificationStatute.description: The participant signs the consolidated petition (signature required; the source records notarization as 'none' and states no verification statute); confirm the current signature and declaration form with counsel and the Clerk-Magistrate.

counselFlags: Never use sealing and expungement interchangeably in Massachusetts copy. Sealing does not destroy the record; expungement does.

Scope threshold: offer this route only where the participant has three or more criminal records from two or more BMC divisions. Below that threshold, use the ordinary judicial sealing route with one form per case.
The consolidated petition supplements rather than replaces the statewide form in BMC.
A counsel-approved custom consolidated petition may be used only for qualifying BMC records. Otherwise use the statewide form per case.
This is a local implementation of the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing remedy, not a separate statewide remedy. Do not double-count the underlying relief mechanism.

Venue: file in the BMC division identified by the Standing Order's residence-based venue rule; a person no longer residing in BMC territory files in the division where the most recent eligible record is from. Confirm the division before filing.

Notice and hearings: a preliminary hearing, public notice and a final hearing follow filing per the Standing Order, and the judge may request additional information or documents about the listed cases from the Clerk-Magistrate or the Probation Department.
Service: per the Standing Order; the source states no separate certificate-of-service component, so none is drafted. Confirm service mechanics with the Clerk-Magistrate.

Verification: the source records the participant's signature as required and notarization as none, and states no verification statute; verificationStatute.citation is left null and the petition carries an ordinary signature and declaration block. Confirm the signature and declaration form with counsel and the Clerk-Magistrate.
Fees: none identified in the review; fee waiver none identified. Confirm with the Clerk-Magistrate.
The good-cause narrative across all listed records is participant-authored through structured prompts against the Pon factors; it must not be drafted for the participant.
Records outside the Boston Municipal Court Department are excluded: this route does not reach District Court, Juvenile Court or Superior Court records.

The participant must obtain their own CORI from the Department of Criminal Justice Information Services and check the case list against it before filing; LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.
The source does not prescribe a caption or party-designation format for the consolidated petition; confirm the caption with the Clerk-Magistrate before filing.

provenance.registryExcerpt: The Boston Municipal Court Department permits a single consolidated petition to seal three or more criminal records from two or more BMC divisions, under a Standing Order revised after Pon to conform to the new legal standard. It is a local implementation of the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing remedy, not a separate statewide remedy. Below the threshold, the ordinary route applies with one form per case. Rules: filing in the BMC division identified by the Standing Order's residence-based venue rule; fees none identified; notice = preliminary hearing, public notice and final hearing per the Standing Order; service per the Standing Order; participant signature required; notarization none. Waiting period: none for dismissal, nolle prosequi, no probable cause or not guilty. Exclusions: records outside the BMC Department; fewer than three records or fewer than two divisions.
